title: Nuclear Chemistry and Chemistry in Everyday Life

questions.question: Radioactivity was discovered in 1896 by:
questions.rationale: Becquerel found that uranium salts fogged photographic plates in the dark; the Curies later isolated polonium and radium.

questions.question: Which radiation has the greatest penetrating power?
questions.rationale: Chargeless, high-energy gamma photons need thick lead or concrete to stop them; paper stops alpha and a few mm of aluminium stops beta.

questions.question: An alpha particle is identical to:
questions.rationale: An alpha particle is ⁴₂He — charge +2, mass 4 u, the most ionizing but least penetrating radiation.

questions.question: The half-life of carbon-14 is about:
questions.rationale: 5,730 years — the clock behind radiocarbon dating, useful for once-living matter up to roughly 50,000 years old.

questions.question: In beta decay:
options: Z rises by 1 while A stays constant
a proton turns into a neutron
questions.rationale: A neutron converts to a proton plus an ejected electron (⁰₋₁e), so the atomic number rises by one at constant mass number.

questions.question: Nuclear reactors keep the fission chain reaction under control using:
questions.rationale: Moderators (water, heavy water, graphite) slow neutrons to fissile speeds while control rods (cadmium, boron) absorb the surplus.

questions.question: The Sun's energy comes from:
questions.rationale: Four hydrogen nuclei fuse into helium, converting mass to energy per E = mc² — fusion, not fission.

questions.question: Smoke detectors commonly rely on which radioactive isotope?
questions.rationale: Americium-241's alpha particles ionize air; smoke interrupts that tiny current and triggers the alarm.

questions.question: Overactive thyroid glands are treated with:
questions.rationale: The thyroid concentrates iodine, so I-131 — with its short 8-day half-life — delivers radiation exactly where needed.

questions.question: CO₂ extinguishers are preferred for electrical fires because CO₂:
options: smothers the fire without conducting electricity or leaving residue
questions.rationale: CO₂ blankets the flames, insulates against current, and leaves no residue — water is dangerous on live circuits.
